course_name_original: Técnicas de ingeniería gráfica aplicadas a ingeniería mecánica
course_name_en: Graphic engineering techniques applied to mechanical engineering

learning_outcomes.text: Students have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated by the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their area of study.
Knowledge and skills to apply graphic engineering techniques.

Advanced spatial vision capability and knowledge of graphic representation techniques, both by traditional methods of metric geometry and descriptive geometry, and by computer-aided design applications.
Ability to work, direct and manage conflicts in a multidisciplinary group and/or a multilingual environment.
Ability for oral and written transmission of information adapted to the audience.
Ability to apply new technologies including information and communication technologies.
Ability for information management, handling and application of technical specifications and necessary legislation for engineering practice.

syllabus_topics: Standardization in specialty drawing and plan creation
Bi-tridimensional geometric drawing in CAD environment
Design and manufacturing engineering. Prototyping techniques
General principles for the representation of elements in the specialty
Representation of plans in the specialty
Topic 3: Generation of graphic documentation using 2D CAD techniques
Topic 4: Three-dimensional drawing: CAD and BIM environments
Generation of graphic documentation using 2D CAD
teaching_methods: Programmed practices in the design and computer laboratory

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and/or participation in face-to-face and/or virtual activities
Theoretical concepts of the subject (theoretical exam, practical cases on CAD system)
Completion of assignments, cases or exercises (4 assignments: 3 individual; 1 group)
Laboratory/field/TIC tool practices (programmed practices on CAD system)

assessment_rules: The grading system will be governed by RD 1125/2003. In the ordinary call, a global evaluation will be carried out including a theoretical-practical evaluation through partial tests, which must achieve a score of 5 points to pass (60% of the final grade). Positive completion of individual and group exercises and programmed CAD practices account for 30% of the final grade. Class attendance and participation will be 10% of the final grade. In extraordinary calls, personal work, attendance, and participation grades and their weights will be maintained, but the theoretical-practical evaluation will be a single final test that must be passed, and partial scores obtained during the course will not be retained.
